title: Chapter 84 — Financing & The Money Conversation
intro: Promotional financing mechanics, the monthly bridge, and the budget conversation with dignity.

sections.title: Financing as a Selling Tool
sections.content:
Financing is not a last resort for customers who cannot afford the purchase. It is a selling tool that makes better products accessible and step-ups painless. Present it proactively on any ticket over $1,500.

The customer who says 'that is a lot' often means 'I do not have that cash right now' — not 'I do not want it.' Financing solves the cash flow problem without reducing the quality of the purchase.

Introduce it during Step 7, after the product is chosen but before the close. 'This comes to $3,200 for the package. We have 12-month no-interest financing — that breaks down to about $267 a month. Would that make the decision easier?'

Never lead with financing before presenting value. The customer needs to want the product before they care about how to pay for it.

sections.title: Framing That Works
sections.content:
Monthly: '$3,200 sounds like a lot. $89 a month for 36 months does not. And at 0 percent for 12 months, the first year costs you nothing in interest.'

Daily: 'That is about $3 a day for a dishwasher that will last 10-15 years. Less than your morning coffee.'

Per-use: 'If you run this dishwasher 5 times a week for 12 years, that is about 12 cents per load for the quietest dishwasher on the market.'

Financing makes step-ups painless. The difference between the 300 series and the 500 series is $400. On 12-month financing, that is an extra $33 a month. For that $33, the customer gets CrystalDry and 4 dBA quieter operation. Present the step-up in monthly terms and the objection dissolves.

For package deals: 'If you finance the whole kitchen package — range, fridge, dishwasher, and hood — the monthly payment is actually less than what most people spend on takeout. And you are upgrading your entire kitchen.'

sections.title: Handling Declined Applications and Budget Conversations
sections.content:
Handle declined applications with dignity. 'No worries — let me see what we can do at your target budget. We have great options at every price point.' Never make them feel embarrassed. Never ask why they were declined. Never let your facial expression change. Simply move to the next solution.

Budget conversations require the same dignity. When a customer says 'I only have $800,' do not show disappointment. Show enthusiasm for what $800 can buy. 'You can get a really solid dishwasher at that budget. Let me show you the best option in that range.'

What NOT to do: Do not ask 'do you need financing?' — it implies they cannot afford it. Do not pressure the application. Do not assume older customers do not want financing — many prefer it for cash flow regardless of ability to pay. Do not announce the minimum purchase for financing loudly enough for other customers to hear.
